title: Exploring Empathy in Individuals With Brain Injury: Psychometric Validation of the Perth Empathy Scale
titleZh: 探索脑损伤个体的共情：珀斯共情量表的心理测量学验证
abstract: Empathy alterations are common after acquired brain injury (ABI), with adverse effects on interpersonal relationships and social reintegration. However, the assessment of empathy remains relatively neglected in clinical settings, since no empathy measures have yet been validated for use in brain-injured populations. As such, this study aimed to psychometrically assess the recently developed Perth Empathy Scale (PES) in an international sample of adults with ABI ( n = 341) and a community sample ( n = 647). Confirmatory factor analyses indicated a theoretically coherent three-factor structure for the PES, comprised of a general cognitive empathy factor and valence-specific affective empathy factors. Measurement invariance was established between ABI and community samples, and results showed good to excellent reliability, concurrent, convergent and discriminant validity. These results help to illuminate the multidimensional nature of the empathy construct in adults with ABI, and suggest that the PES is a robust measure of empathy in this population.
